name: Toepen
description: Toepen is a Dutch no-trump last-trick game for 3-8 players. Stakes increase through knocking, which forces fold-or-stay decisions and turns each four-trick hand into a bluffing and risk-management contest.
deck: 32-card French pack (10, 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J in each suit)

history.origins: Toepen is a long-standing Dutch social game, often played as a drinking or pub game, and is closely related to German regional forms such as Tuppen and Siwweschroom.
timeline: Traditional play: Established in Dutch social circles as a fast last-trick game.
Tournament era: Formalized procedures for knocking and folding appear in organized play.
Present: Continues in both serious and drinking-table formats.
history.cultural: Its social identity comes from table talk, bluffing, and timing pressure around immediate fold decisions after knocks.
history.evolution: The core rules remained stable: 32 cards, unusual 10-high rank order, no trumps, and stake escalation by knocking.

setup.players: 3-8 players in clockwise order; dealer rotates.
setup.deck: 32-card deck with rank 10 (high), 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J (low). No trumps.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 4 cards to each player. Player left of dealer leads first trick.
setup.equipment: Cards and a life/penalty score tracker.

rules.objective: Avoid hand penalties by winning the fourth (last) trick, or by folding at favorable moments when stakes rise.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Deal**: Four cards each. 2. **Tricks**: Play four tricks; players must follow suit if possible, otherwise may play any card. Highest card of led suit wins and leads next trick. 3. **Knocking**: After players have viewed cards, and at any time during the hand, a player may knock to raise stake by one. 4. **Responses**: Other players choose to stay in or fold; folded players lose current stake and stop participating in the hand. 5. **Result**: Winner of trick four avoids hand loss; other staying players lose according to total stake.
keyRules: Only the fourth trick decides the hand winner.
Knocking raises stake for everyone still active.
The last player to knock cannot knock again until someone else has knocked.
A player cannot knock and fold to that same knock.

strategy.basic: Preserve suit control for trick four; do not waste strongest cards on low-impact early tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Fold discipline is critical: conceding early can be optimal when your trick-four equity is poor under high stakes.
strategy.advanced: Use conditional knocks: raise after opponents commit high cards or show suit weakness, maximizing fold equity and expected penalty gain.
tips: Track remaining 10s since they dominate each suit.
If you can guarantee trick four after seeing earlier plays, knocking before revealing strength is often profitable.
At high score pressure, opponents over-fold; exploit that with selective bluffs.

variations.name: Fast Drinking Response
variations.description: After a knock, players fold immediately (simultaneous tempo); hesitation counts as staying in.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes response timing only; no engine constant overrides documented.

variations.name: Ordered Tournament Response
variations.description: After a knock, responses proceed in turn starting left of the knocker.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes response order only; no engine constant overrides documented.

variations.name: Elimination Continuation
variations.description: After one player reaches 10 points and drops out, others continue until one player remains.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes game end condition; no engine constant overrides documented.

scoring.description: Penalty-life system where baseline loss is 1 life and each knock increases effective stake by 1.
scoring.winCondition: In standard round play, game ends when a player reaches 10 lives and loses the rubber; elimination variants continue until one player remains.

synthesis.shortDescription: A four-trick no-trump game where knocks turn small mistakes into big losses.
